subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Janelle / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Concern about PII surfacing in inference logs (esp. free-text prompts/responses).
- Need for configurable retention windows and proof of deletion for regulated data.
- Requirement for immutable audit logs for compliance and e-discovery.
- Ability to redact or block certain fields at ingestion (PHI/SSNs) and avoid them being stored in any logs or cache.

Current stack notes you mentioned:
- Ingest & product run on AWS (us-west-2).
- Contractual requirement to keep raw PII retention <= 90 days and maintain audit logs for 7+ years.
- Existing SIEM pulls logs from vendor endpoints; you’d prefer pushing audit logs to an ACME-managed S3 bucket.

Success criteria you’ll use to evaluate us (at a high level):
1) Demonstrable PII redaction at ingestion and no PII in stored token logs.
2) Support for customer-managed KMS/HSM for any key material.
3) Configurable retention policy per dataset and capability to export immutable audit logs.
4) Documentation and artifacts (SOC 2, redaction policy, dataflow diagram) for procurement/security review.

Next steps / asks from us:
- I’ll share our SOC 2 redacted report, a sample redaction policy, and a data-flow diagram (attaching via follow-up).
- Can you confirm the specific retention windows/SLAs you need (you mentioned 90 days for raw PII, 7 years for audit logs)?
- Propose follow-up technical sync with your infra/security team — are you available next Tue (11/3) or Wed (11/4) morning PT?

Action items for me: share docs + loop in our engineering lead to confirm feasibility and delivery timeline.

Thanks — talk soon.

Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap, Dylan — that matches what we discussed. A couple more specifics from our security & compliance side: 

- Retention: our baseline is 90 days max for any raw PII. Audit logs must be retained for 7 years and be tamper-evident.
- Redaction: we need field-level redaction at ingestion (we don’t want SSNs, financial account numbers, or full patient names to ever be stored or cached).
- Keys: vendor must support customer-managed KMS; if HSM-backed key control is required we can discuss that as part of procurement.
- Auditability: we need to receive a continuous stream or periodic exports of immutable audit logs to our S3 (or be able to query them via secure API).
- Evidence: please include SOC2 type II (most recent), encryption at-rest/in-transit docs, and a sample redaction policy for our reviewers.

We’ll also need to validate that your runtime won’t write PII into internal logs or vendor analytics. Can you confirm whether token-level logs are stored by default and whether they can be disabled/hashed?

I can make time for the follow-up on Wed 11/4 9–11am PT. Invite our infra lead (Tom) and our security manager (Iccia A.).

Appreciate it — Janelle

Hi team — quick technical summary and what we can provide by EOD today (attaching stubs):

What Redwood supports today:
- PII redaction: We support configurable ingestion pipelines that apply field-level redaction (regex and ML-based recognizers) prior to tokenization. Redacted fields are replaced and never stored in plaintext in token logs or cached KV by default.
- KV cache / runtime cache: We can disable KV cache persistence per-customer and we have a hardened path that prevents sensitive fields from being cached.
- Token-level logs: By default we capture anonymized telemetry; token-level request/response logs can be disabled and we can optionally hash or redact tokens before any persistent logging.
- Retention: Configurable retention policies per dataset — can enforce 90-day max for raw PII and separate 7-year retention for append-only audit logs.
- Audit logs: We can stream audit logs (immutable, append-only) to customer-managed S3 buckets with server-side encryption. Logs include timestamped actions, request identifiers, and non-PII metadata required for compliance.
- Keys: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) and can integrate with customer HSMs where required; we can provide architecture notes for a dedicated key envelope flow.

Artifacts we are attaching (stubs):
- SOC2_report_redwood_v3.pdf — redacted SOC2 type II report (latest)
- redaction_policy_sample.docx — our sample redaction policy and detection rules
- redwood-dataflow-diagram.png — high-level dataflow showing where redaction and audit logging occur

Open items (we should discuss on 11/4):
- Exact audit-log schema ACME needs for e-discovery (we can map existing fields).
- SSO/SAML onboarding and SCIM provisioning (for procurement).
- Any legal data residency clauses beyond us-west-2.

Proposed attendees: Dev Patel (engineering), Marissa Cole (security sales), Dylan Brooks (AE), Janelle Wu, Tom Rivera, Iccia A. (ACME security).

If this looks good I’ll attach the artifacts to the HubSpot record and share a calendar invite for Wed 11/4 9:30am PT.
